brands.description: The Print Shop is a basic desktop publishing software package developed in the early 1980s by Brøderbund. It was unique in that it provided libraries of clip-art and templates through a simple interface to build signs, posters and banners with household dot-matrix printers. Over the years the software has been updated to accommodate changing file formats and printer technologies.
brands.name: The Print Shop

An extended ZIP+4 code was introduced in 1983 which includes the five digits of the ZIP Code, followed by a hyphen and four additional digits that reference a more specific location.

transcript.text: Hello, welcome to Onprint Shop.
In this tutorial, we'll walk you through all the exciting new features and enhancements introduced in version 12.2.
In our previous version, we introduced configurable products in offline quotes.
With version 12.2, we're extending this functionality to offline orders as well.
When adding a new offline order, admins will now see a new product type configurable.
After selecting this type, they can define the product details and add product options.
Options can be added one by one manually or pulled in quickly from preset options by selecting A tag.
Custom options with pricing can also be added here, while irrelevant options can be removed from the list to simplify the setup.
The price summary instantly updates to display the cost in real time based on the chosen options.
Before saving, the Validate Rules button helps admins check if any option rules apply to the selected options.
If rules are detected, admins can either keep them as is or override them for this specific order, ensuring complete flexibility.
Next up, let's talk about pricing.
With a new tier based pricing feature, admins can create flexible pricing strategies tailored to different customer groups.
This is managed by first creating Markup Masters and then defining pricing tiers.
These tiers can then be assigned to customer groups, whether globally or at the product level.
This makes it easier to serve retail customers, resellers, and B2B clients with differential pricing all from one streamlined system.
Talking about the next one, we've simplified the checkout process for guest customers.
For example, if a customer chooses local pickup, they no longer need to provide a shipping address.
By skipping unnecessary steps, orders can be completed much faster, creating a smoother buying experience.
Moving on to quotes, managing them is now much easier.
Admins can filter quotes by sales agent or printer, and sales agent details now appear directly in the quote itself.
While placing an offline quote, admins also have the flexibility to apply or bypass master option rules using the Validate Rules button, reducing the chances of errors.
In addition, when adding existing products to quotes, the system now fetches prices for all quantities, not just the first.
It also auto fills production days for extra quantities and vendor prices for master options on the Quote Action page, helping save time and minimize manual entry.
Shipping and Logistics have received some powerful upgrades in version 12.2.
Let's look at the enhancement made to the Local Pickup from Store shipping method.
Previously, product specific shipping settings were applied globally across all pickup locations.
With this update, admins can now define product specific shipping at the local pickup address level, allowing better control over which products are available at each store.
A new toggle called Product Assignment by Address has been added under the Local Pickup method.
When disabled, default product specific rules apply globally.
When enabled, these rules can be set individually for each pickup address.
The same configuration options used at the method level now appear on the Local Pickup Address edit screen for consistency.
For example, if business cards are available only at the Radix House and posters at the Katlia Print House, customers will see only the relevant pickup location during checkout.
Radix House for business cards and Katlia Print House for posters.
The shipping cost by order subtotal method is now more flexible with support for both percentage based pricing and zone specific rules.
Earlier, this method only supported flat shipping charges based on subtotal ranges.
With a new update, the admin can now configure shipping costs as a fixed amount or a percentage of the cart subtotal and even define separate rules for different shipping zones.
This gives admins greater flexibility to align shipping strategies with business and regional requirements.
On the Shipping Method edit page, under Shipping Settings, the admin will find a new option called Shipping Price Setup.
By default, it's set to Amount Dollar, applying flat rates as before.
Switching it to Percentage Percent symbol allows the system to calculate shipping as a percentage of the order subtotal.
For example, entering 5% on a $100 order applies a $5 shipping fee, and for a $300 order it automatically adjusts to $15, ensuring shipping scales with the order value.
Additionally, the admin can also enable zone based pricing to apply different shipping rates by region.
When disabled, the system uses the default zone rates globally.
When enabled, it matches the customer's address to a defined zone and applies that zones pricing.
If no match is found, the default zone rates are used.
If none exist, the method won't appear at checkout.
We have introduced A functionality use Printer as shipper.

When enabled, the system will calculate shipping rates and generate shipping labels using the printer specific ship from address, ensuring shipments reflect the correct origin with carriers like UPS and FedEx.
If disabled, the system will continue to use the company's primary address from general settings to manage shipping scenarios more accurately.
Most importantly, shipping rates now consider product dimensions, material thickness, box weight, and extra space, leading to smarter packaging and more accurate charges.
This enhancement is applicable only to custom size products where the sheet or rigid option is selected.

For example, for the custom size product vinyl banner, the system will consider the package product weight, box weight, material thickness, box dimensions, as well as the additional space while calculating the shipping package.
This ensures that shipping charges are based on the actual package size, avoiding underestimation or overestimation.
Let's look at another admin side improvement.
A new bulk assignment feature now allows admins to assign master options or attributes to multiple products in one go.
This significantly reduces manual effort and ensures consistency across your catalog.
The interface also shows the number of products to which the options are being assigned, making bulk operations more transparent.
Continuing with product key enhancements, galleries are now more visual and informative.
Multiple images can be linked to each attribute or option combination.

For example, if you want to display multiple examples of business cards with Spot UV finishing, you can upload multiple images for the single attribute, Spot UV in this case, and customers can now see the effect of this finishing on multiple cards.
On the storefront side, we've added more convenience.
Customers can now search their saved designs by product name and size.
This makes it easier for them to find and reuse past work, saving both time and effort.
Another update for the storefront is the improved display of dynamic templates.
Options such as folds and orientations are now shown more clearly, helping customers pick the right template with confidence.
Finally, product titles inside the shopping cart are now clickable.
This means customers can jump directly to the product details page from the cart, improving navigation and overall usability.
And that wraps up part one of our On Print Shop Version 12.2 features tutorial.
We covered major updates like configurable products in offline orders, tier based pricing, Smarter checkout, shipping enhancements, and storefront usability improvements.
Be sure to check out Part 2, where we'll continue exploring the remaining functionalities of this exciting release.
If you have any questions, our support team is always here to help.
You can reach us via live chat or e-mail us at support onprintshop.com.
